The Precious Instructions of the Lotus Land, Part Two:
The Precious Instructions of the World-Honored One Śākyamuni and Amitābha (Originally one hundred ten poems; now twenty-odd have been selected and preserved).
Humble and lowly official serving in Yuling, I am ashamed to bear the title of "Flower-Seal" over a hundred-li domain. For my entire life, I have been upright and sincere.
Nature. Morning after morning, recite the Buddha’s name to cross over the dark realm. I, the City God of Gaoyou, find that the Buddha’s power is impartial and my own courage chilled.
Questioning my heart, I am without shame and my mind finds peace; only then do I feel ashamed that I have not yet fully repaid the nation through loyalty and filial piety.

I must urgently advance to the platform for holding the name of the Buddha. I, the Earth Deity of Gaoyou, see that hell has no gate, yet in truth it does. Rebirth and retribution follow one another in a cycle.
At that time, although Amitābha possesses boundless power, it is difficult to save sentient beings who suffer from ignorance.

I am the Judge of the Underworld; though my heart desires tranquility, my mind finds no rest. I toil tirelessly between heaven and the human realm. Yet the wicked remain as numerous as the branches of a tall tree.
I wish to take that tall tree and prune its branches one by one. I serve as the assistant to Lin Hong of the Forest of Cyclic Existence for a thousand years.

The resentment of enmity is difficult to dispel; with a single point of loyal heart, I protect the Han dynasty. When affairs reach their end, they are hard to turn back; in vain, my crimson blood stains the azure blade.
I, Guan Yu of the Han, dwelt in the celestial realm before arriving in the human world; only today do I realize how difficult it is to transcend this world.
While the palace towers are illuminated by the brilliance of luminous pearls, how can they compare to crossing through the pass of worldly passions? I, [Guan Yu]...
The four celestial lords and their retinues arrive, borne upon palanquins draped in ethereal heavenly robes. At the height of the five clouds, the ninefold gates open wide;

those wearing crowns and holding ceremonial tablets follow the golden sovereign, chanting the Great Name in unison to sow the seeds of merit. I, the Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, see that the forms of mountains and rivers are all empty and illusory.
To recognize the return to the source is to find one’s true home; through diligent recitation of the Name, one must awaken to this truth for oneself.
To avoid being left desolate and lingering at the ends of the earth. I examine the young novices: the three teachings return to their source, which is fundamentally emptiness;

once the three births are liberated, all conditions are penetrated. To awaken to the fundamental root is true awakening; such a state of "as-it-is" (tathatā) is not easily encountered. I oversee the altar with single-minded sincerity;
forging iron into steel through the thought of single-minded sincerity, I come from the East to ferry the multitudes across the ocean of karma.
Birth. Through the power of Amitābha’s boundless mindfulness, the ground of the mind becomes perfectly luminous and vows are spontaneously fulfilled.
I, Huang Daitie, see a dilapidated temple where the weeds grow green; there are only a few fireflies visible in the vast sky.

When the day comes that the light of wisdom shines universally, the clouds of compassion and the rain of Dharma will pervade the Fragrant Pavilion. I, Master Lianchi, [observe how] worldly people create karma and are trapped in Saṃsāra.
O, how can one endure being submerged for so many years? Hasten to practice diligently so as to reach the other shore. Like the shuttle of a loom, the months and years are easily consumed.

My King, may you find rest in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, a realm of joy where celestial flowers fall in profusion like jade ornaments, and the sounds of the Dharma are chanted in harmonious unison.
Trees, birds, ponds, and flowing streams all join in proclaiming the truth. This is my Venerable Master Huiyuan.

How can one enter meditative concentration? By diligently reciting the Buddha’s name. This Mahāyāna skillful means is easy to practice; with a single mind free from distraction, one returns to emptiness and stillness.

Thus, one naturally attains rebirth within a lotus womb, entrusted to a precious pond. My late Master, the Venerable Sheng’an, spread the Dharma rain and clouds of compassion throughout the great thousandfold world.

Though I ascend the altar, it is difficult to fully proclaim his virtuous words. Those who are deluded, stubborn, and inverted have minds like those of the intoxicated; who among them is willing to return together with me?
The Lotus of the Seven Jewels. I, Master Yongming, say: Human life passes too easily—these are but three springs.
Do not let the bonds of emotional attachments enslave your entire life. Sweep away mental affairs within the mind; refine the dream-body within the dream. I am Mañjuśrī.
There is a path to the Land of Lotuses, yet no one recognizes it. The jewel-mirror is free of dust and shines eternally through the long night. Alas for the river of karma!
"O disciples, when shall your merit be fulfilled so that you may emerge from the red dust of the mundane world? I am Samantabhadra. Within this flask is the cool flavor of nectar;
in my hand I hold a bright pearl of a hundred jewels' radiance. Upon the tips of willow branches, wisdom blossoms.

From this moment on, with a single sprinkling, you shall be freed from calamity and misfortune. I am an old monk from the South Sea. In hand I grasp fresh lotus leaves, planted with deliberate care. Through this cultivation and practice, I make my vow."
This is sufficient proof for the Lotus Throne. Although I have now attained fruition in Sukhāvatī this morning, it was due to my pure karma from years past.
I, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, emerge from the tranquil light as ten thousand golden lotuses; why do sentient beings abandon their native home?
If they can return to the root and revert to the original essence, they will behold the majestic Great Dharma King—I am he, Śākyamuni, the Elder. Silence.
The old dhūta within the radiant land; beneath the sixteen-foot golden body, he crosses the river of karma.
With a precious raft, he spans the boundless ocean of vows, relying solely on his original vow to deliver the Sahā world. This is none other than our Dharma-treasury Bhikṣu.

Countless kalpas ago, we established great vows that the Dharma would be transmitted to the Eastern Land to universally deliver all sentient beings. It was because of the turbid evil and ignorance [of the age]... for a long time.
Adrift in the ocean of delusive karma, we sons of the Buddha seek to rescue the great trichiliocosm and together escape the wheel of suffering.

Now, the Pure Buddha has established this society to transform and guide worldly people, so that we may collectively cultivate the True Dharma and universally practice mindfulness of the Buddha. Our merit and practice are already vast;
yet we must constantly polish ourselves and rouse our spirits. Once we attain the state where the mind is undisturbed and grasp our original face, we shall know the Buddha.

What I have said is not false. I have now descended to this site of enlightenment because the sentient beings of this land bear heavy karmic offenses and the great kalpa of destruction is about to come to pass;

I truly feel deep compassion for them. In those regions where the calamity of slaughter has not yet struck, there are two or three virtuous men and women who, on behalf of all sentient beings, recite the Buddha’s name and perform sincere repentance.
Now you must all give rise to the Great Vow and open the practice of the Nianfo Chan (Buddha-Recitation Repentance). 4.
The nineteenth day. I have prepared this memorial with profound grief and earnestness. This matter concerns the great destiny of the realm; it must not be treated as a trivial pastime.
Whether the kalpa-period shall endure or end depends entirely upon the resonance of a single thought. Be cautious, be cautious!
The Precious Instructions of the Tathāgata Dharmaprabhāsa of the Past (originally consisting of over ten stanzas, now abridged).

You have completed the forty-nine-day period of repentance. The light of your minds has gathered into a perfect sphere, continuing in an unbroken succession with the great compassionate light of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Yet, during this repentance, there were still fifteen individuals whose spirits were unsettled and their minds distracted.

During that interval, few will be delivered from suffering and calamity; even the slightest misfortune cannot be avoided. You all possess eyes of karma and ears of karma; thus you neither see nor hear.
Within the repentance rites, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas manifest countless billions of bodies corresponding to the various realms of existence, communicating in their respective languages.

Whether in the Celestial Bureaus or the Netherworld, on islands or in the Dragon Palaces, or within the sites of practice where one hears the sutras and listens to the Buddhas, may all grudges and transgressions be resolved to extinguish the great kalpas.
The Buddhas, out of their compassionate hearts for sentient beings, would rather grind their own bones to dust than find it easy to repay even a ten-thousandth part of this kindness.
Each of you should bow toward the West to express gratitude for the Buddha’s grace; each of you should bow toward the void to express gratitude for the protection [of the Dharma].
To all the devas and nāgas:
In the third or fourth year of the Tongzhi era, I frequently dreamed of great floods during the night, yet I did not consider them unusual.
However, in the fifth year, I dreamed that waves surged across the entire earth with no discernible shore, and heaven and earth were shrouded in darkness; raindrops fell like eggs. Suddenly—

Seeing water and other leaks from the eaves, he hurriedly climbed onto the roof; losing his footing, he fell and was startled awake. He marveled at this deeply. The following day, he suspended the spirit-writing board (*jī*) to request a divine revelation.
Out of the compassion of all the Buddhas, there was subsequently a decree to open a Universal Buddha Dharma-Assembly (*pǔfó dàochǎng*) to avert the calamity of the kalpa.
I and my fellow practitioners began this sincere repentance ceremony. On the third day of the repentance, I was struck with a severe fever accompanied by chills, and sores broke out all over my body.
At every prostration, my skin felt as if it were being sliced by a knife. Enduring these ailments, I continued the service for more than forty days without giving rise to any regret or backsliding.
When the repentance was completed, my illness also quickly subsided. A Bodhisattva of Single-Sincerity judged and declared: "You all..."

To undertake this repentance ceremony was to shoulder an exceedingly heavy burden; thus, he encountered demonic obstacles and setbacks. Fortunately, his aspiration for Bodhi was so earnest that he did not cease midway—this is truly worthy of reverence and praise.

From the commencement of the repentance until the thirty-fifth day, the upper river embankment breached by over two hundred *zhang*, and all the large and small embankments of the lower river's marshes collapsed.
The landscape stretched out as a vast expanse of water reaching the heavens; yet, the disaster was but a hair’s breadth away from becoming total ruin.
It was thus. Had the disaster been total, one could not have known what the scene would have looked like. Yet there were still signs of divine response:
the Shengde Weir where I reside is forty *li* in circumference and contains over thirty thousand *mu* of paddy fields.

While all the other weirs had breached, this weir alone remained standing tall. When the waters reached it, they already levelled the top of the embankment and were on the verge of flooding through; suddenly, a violent...

A great wind arose, uprooting trees and tearing down houses. At that time, the sound of the wind and the water, mingled with the sounds of many men laboring to build embankments and their cries of lamentation, were so heart-stirring and soul-shaking that those performing the ritual repentance could not remain steadfast.

They sought guidance by supporting the spirit-medium’s rod (*luan*), and the judgment declared: "All those at the altar should settle their minds, return to their seats, and recite the Buddha's name. This is the influence of the six desires."
The celestial Māras exercise their majesty; because of this, for several days your mental radiance has gathered into a sphere. They intend to use their awesome power to damage your site of practice.
You should simply withdraw and stabilize your minds; do not give rise to groundless doubt or fear. I grant you one talisman; hang it within the altar.
This shall protect you so that demonic obstacles are transformed into auspiciousness, and afflictions are turned into purity.

Peace. Cherish this well. When the wind is slight at the beginning of the *zi* hour, and the water is perfectly still at the start of the *chou* hour, the embankment is easily secured and the waters immediately recede.
Thus, this paddy field not only escapes disaster but also yields an abundant harvest.
That such a response occurs through the convergence of the Way is truly inconceivable. (Zhàoluán) respectfully records this.
Shou Tan’s *Horizontal Transcendence Bodhisattva Precious Instructions*:
"The single phrase of Amitābha transcends birth and death; when recitation is perfected, one beholds the Dharma King. Ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes of enmity are all released;
in a single instant, one smiles and realizes the Lotus Land. Horizontal transcendence surpasses [the gradual path]. Pure Buddha. Formerly, in my life, I was a cloth merchant. Six.

For ten years, he has traded with absolute honesty, refusing to shortchange others by even a fraction of an inch. He maintains the *Cundī* fast, practices the release of living beings (*fangsheng*), and observes the precept against killing;

thus, after death, he shall be free from transgression. Furthermore, he possesses deep faith in the Pure Land and has come here to guard this altar. Our Buddha opened this gate of "transcending horizontally" through the recitation of the Buddha's name (*nianfo*).

Yet, worldly karmic consciousness is profoundly deep, and people often do not believe in it. Recently, however, the cultivation of pure karma (*jingye*) has flourished greatly within the realm of the dead.
Dharma assemblies for the recitation of the Buddha’s name have been established at various local City God temples; there are already nine hundred and thirty such locations.
Generally, it is after seventy-seven days have passed since a person in the world has died that their worldly good and evil deeds are examined and they receive their respective karmic retributions.

Any soul-essence that has not yet been assigned its destination within these forty-nine days is immediately sent into these dharma assemblies to recite the Buddha’s name. If one is sincere and free from doubt, [the benefit will be realized].
Thus, one may immediately resolve karmic grievances and be reborn in Sukhāvatī. If one lacks deep faith, one will continue as before in saṃsāra, receiving retribution according to one's karma.
Pure Buddha, you should know that the Buddhas of the void have established a single *maṇḍala* with golden tiles and jade pillars, lapis lazuli and precious steps;
its palaces reach up to the Nakṣatra Heaven, where Buddhas and Bodhisattvas constantly come to preach the Dharma.
Celestial immortals from the upper realms came to this site of practice to take refuge and receive the precepts, each vowing to attain Bodhicitta.

Through the sincere instructions of the Bodhisattva Yicheng, the Buddha-Dharma flourished greatly in the realm of darkness. The Great Emperor of the Eastern Peak also established a Buddha-recitation site to guide departed souls.
[The Judge] said: "All those before the altar of the City God who do not recite the Buddha's name shall undergo infernal punishments and be sent to Mount Dongyue several times.
If they do recite the Buddha's name, they shall be sent to a great place of practice to repent for their sins and attain rebirth in the Pure Land.

If they again do not believe, they shall be handed over to King Yama, who will weigh the lightness or gravity of the three karmas of body, speech, and mind committed during their life in the world of the living, and assign them to one of the three miserable realms."
In response to their retribution, there is no foreseeable end to their suffering. The Buddhas take pity on sentient beings;

furthermore, because Elder Wuhé expounded the Dharma-door of the hidden realm, he attained resonance with the spirits of the underworld. Consequently, each of the deities gave rise to the aspiration for enlightenment and attained liberation from birth and death.
This is the fixed number of causes and conditions from kalpas past; this number is known clearly only by the Buddha. We have not yet realized the five eyes or the six supernatural powers.
One does not know the causes and conditions from immeasurable kalpas past. [Recite] the *Purifying Buddha-Practice, Emptiness-Purgatory, and Resolving Enmity Great Repentance*.

Contemplate all Buddhas for seven days each; within these fourteen days, rely upon the vows and majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to illuminate you, the disciples in this dharma assembly.
From immeasurable kalpas ago, regarding the countless bodies you have received, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—[one...]

First, they manifest immeasurable bodies of various kinds, emitting great radiance that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, reaching upward to the Peak of Existence (*bhavāgra*) and downward to the Avīci Hell.

They communicate with them in their own tongues, exhorting them to recollect the Buddha, and gathering them to this site of practice to hear the sutra, listen to the Buddha, perform prostrations and repentance, and receive food.
Thus, they awaken them from delusion, dissolve their grievances and enmity, and cause them to repent their karmic offenses. Awaken!
The awakened one naturally recites the Buddha’s name. With each single recitation of the Buddha’s name, a ray of light is emitted. This light is the primordial light inherent within sentient beings;
however, because they have transmigrated through the six realms of existence and their karmic offenses are profound, this light remains unrevealed, and they thus become sentient beings.
As for the immortals and seers of the upper realms: some ascend due to great loyalty or great filial piety; some ascend through the practice of alchemical refinement;

and some ascend by cultivating the ten superior wholesome deeds. Their original radiance remains unrevealed, and when their merit is exhausted, they undergo cyclic rebirth, unable to transcend the three realms.

Such beings are also called sentient beings; they possess the physical forms of the two paths of the underworld spirits and ghosts, as well as the three miserable states of hell-dwellers and hungry ghosts.

The retribution bodies of animals and other such beings are diverse in their manifestations, yet all are called sentient beings. Beyond the three realms, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are the Dharma-body.
In this ritual of the Dharma-assembly for repentance, you should contemplate the light of the Buddha’s mindfulness.

The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas universally radiate light, and the soul-consciousness of all sentient beings likewise contemplates the light of the Buddha’s mindfulness. These lights continue one after another in an unbroken succession.
The Great Radiant Banner of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas enshrouds the soul-consciousness within the seven realms of existence, causing it to transcend the three worlds and cross the Golden Bridge.
It traverses ten trillion Buddha-lands in the time it takes to snap one's fingers, arriving at the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

However, if sentient beings harbor thoughts of envy or deluded attachment as they pass through these various lands, they will descend back to the Buddha-lands they have traversed and fail to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Thus it is said: "If one gives rise to a single thought of envy, one shall not attain rebirth in that land."

The Buddha-lands are joyful, immeasurable, and boundless. Outside the lotus ponds, there are the adornments of the City of Doubt, which are even more magnificent than the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven of the Desire Realm.
Beyond that, there was once the city of Tālamiśra, the City of Transformation, and the Land of Indolence;

only after passing these does one reach the lotus ponds and enter the Land of Common Abode for Ordinary Beings and Sages. Advancing further, one enters the Land of Skillful Means with Remainder. Advancing yet further, one enters the Land of True Reward Adornments.

Adorning the land. One further advances to the Land of Eternal Quiescent Light (*nitya-prabhāsvara*). For those who cultivate the pure practices, once they attain single-mindedness without distraction, all the realms they encounter will not stir their thoughts;
their consciousness may then directly surge upward into the Land of Eternal Quiescent Light, entering the Jewel Pond and casting themselves into the lotus womb.

When the flower opens, they behold the Buddha. However, if they encounter illusory transformations such as the city of doubt and allow their thoughts to waver, they will immediately fall into a peripheral realm within the lotus womb.
One must practice through kalpas before the flowers finally bloom and one may behold the Buddha. There, the opening and closing of the lotus flowers constitutes a single day and night;
what is already but a minor kalpa in the Sahā world is here measured differently. I now clearly declare this to be my compassion. Exert yourselves!
Regarding those who attain rebirth: the stages are determined by the depth of one's power on the Path.

A single day of practice in this Sahā world surpasses a thousand years in the Western Land; for while this place is purely evil, that place is entirely good, and thus their meritorious practices are distinguished.
During your fourteen days of repentance, all that you have saved are the karmic conditions—both good and evil—of people throughout their successive lifetimes. As for what is called "good":
As for "conditions" (*pratyaya*): they may have previously been your parents, teachers, elders, relatives, or friends;
or they may have once received your aid and protection. These are your virtuous conditions (*kuśala-pratyaya*). As for so-called "unwholesome conditions" (*akuśala-pratyaya*):

they may be creditors or enemies from your past lives, or those whom you mistakenly injured or intentionally killed. Because their transgressions are grave, they receive the retribution of animal bodies. Not...

They are able to take revenge. Once their retribution for past offenses is exhausted, they are reborn as human beings. Because they were previously killed by you, this constitutes your own evil condition.
Both good and evil conditions exist within a single sentient being, and all sentient beings likewise possess them in relation to one another.
Thus, with immeasurable and boundless conditions of both good and evil, one circulates and receives retributions within the three realms without end.
In an instant one is a spirit or ghost; in an instant a king, noble, general, or minister; in an instant a poor person or lowly servant; and in an instant a being in hell or an animal.
Tumbling and turning upside down, one may previously have been a mother and later become a daughter, or previously have been a son and later become a father, or...
Formerly we were brothers; later you became an animal. Your elder brother returned to the human path, yet you, as his younger brother, became food for him.
Ordinary people change their heads and faces, thereby confusing cause and effect. When the Buddhas observe this, they grieve in secret. Is it not something to be feared?
You asked me about my origins before the Pure Buddha, but I did not immediately tell you. Now that the ritual affairs within the altar have been concluded and there is leisure, I shall tell you.

I was a jinshi (provincial graduate) during the Song dynasty. I had no desire to serve in the imperial court. From my youth, I have delighted in reciting the Buddha’s name, practicing the release of living beings, and maintaining a vegetarian diet.
Every day I recite the Buddha’s name five thousand times, and once every month I release living beings. When I reached the age of fifty-eight, I made a vow to travel to Putuo Mountain.
When he traveled to Shandong, he met a monk named Xingyue, who asked him what his lifelong occupation had been. He replied, "I have never served in office;
my greatest delight has been the Buddha. The monk said, "When you recite the Buddha’s name, whom do you take as your object of mindfulness? He replied, "My greatest delight has been the Buddha."
Unaware of what he was thinking, the Upādhyāya sighed and said, "I observe that your body emits light for more than a fathom;
how could I have known you were still a suffering being of this Sahā world? I asked the reason, and the Upādhyāya revealed to me the skillful means of the Pure Land Dharma-gate.
He further presented me with a copy of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* and two volumes of his recorded sayings, which explain entirely the Western World of Ultimate Bliss. I—
Prostrating myself in refuge, I was granted the name Yicheng. I lived until the age of ninety-three before my passing.

I was received by the Great Being Avalokiteśvara to be reborn in the Western Paradise, where I entered a lotus womb. My lotus flower has a circumference of forty li, corresponding to the roads of this world;
among the lotuses of Sukhāvatī, it is the lowest. For several hundred years, I have remained within this lotus womb.
In my practice of Buddha-remembrance and repentance, I ultimately failed to penetrate the two characters of "single-minded sincerity" (yīchéng).

After the Great Being Avalokiteśvara preached the Dharma for me several times, my karmic obstructions were entirely eliminated and my true nature was awakened and clarified. Flowers blossomed as I beheld the Buddha, who placed his hand upon my head and bestowed a prediction of enlightenment.

Thus, I was born in the lowest grade of the lowest level within the Land of Common Abode of Ordinary Beings and Sages. This was because while I was in the world, I only cultivated my own self and did not know to bring forth [the aspiration for others].
"May you deliver the world. Alas, some fall into the Lesser Vehicle; now, to purify the Buddha’s patience and diligence and to give rise to such vast and great vows of compassion is truly admirable.
This is the "Precious Instruction of the Single-Sincerity Bodhisattva" for presiding over the altar.
I am one in sincerity. Hehe! Although this place of practice is small, it is known throughout the Sahā world.
Your merit from bestowing cinnabar for seven days is worthy of respect and praise. Throughout the ten directions and immeasurable lands, among the sentient beings of the six realms—

The benefits received are immeasurable. However, it is regrettable that the cultivation of meritorious practices has not been profound and the power of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) is insufficient;

thus, the light of the mind cannot be gathered into a perfect sphere, and the spiritual elixir of liberation cannot manifest infinite transformations. There still remain eight hundred million lands where this merit has not yet been attained.
This is like those people who have achieved the practice of "one mind undisturbed" (*ekacitta-avikṣipta*); when they recite mantras and refine the elixir, they emit [light].

At that time, without giving rise to a single deluded thought, a single grain of cinnabar— relying upon the power of the Buddha and the power of mantras— can transform into hundreds, thousands, tens of millions, billions, even trillions of grains.
This is the precious instruction of the Bodhisattva for guarding the altar with purity and breadth.

I am Pure and Vast. In this *Jingfo dengxing xiaozai chan* (Repentance for Eliminating Calamities through the Equal Practices of the Pure Buddhas), although one cannot eliminate all calamities entirely, by relying on the Buddha’s compassion, they may be reduced by half.
Friends, do you know the benefits of reciting the Buddha’s name? Reciting the Buddha’s name does not benefit oneself alone;
it simultaneously benefits others. To benefit others is itself to benefit oneself; fundamentally, there is no distinction between them. Now, together with you all—
I shall provide several analogies to explain this. Suppose there is a house of three bays, and within that house, you are all debtors with equal obligations.

Creditors pursue you without ceasing; even if you were to repay everything at once, it would not suffice. If you wish to flee, you are intercepted; you must repay each and every debt before you can leave.
Once the debts are cleared, no one inside the house will stop you, and you may walk out by yourselves. These three bays of the house represent the Three Realms.
The debtors within the house are bound by the causes and conditions of your successive lives; you must repay each and every one of them.
Once the debts are cleared and the debtors have left the house, you shall hear the sound and light of our recitation of the Buddha’s name, which universally delivers all karmic affinities.

When these affinities transcend the three realms, there will be no one remaining within the house. Your departure from the house signifies that after this life you shall be reborn in the Western Pure Land. This is the general path.
Recite the Buddha’s name in this place regardless of wind or rain; you must, in all cases, attend the altar.

Through the majestic power and radiance of the Buddha, the karmic affinities within the realm of darkness will be severed one day earlier, and you will be reborn in the Western Pure Land one day sooner. At the time of death, you will naturally be free from the coming and going of karmic creditors to entangle you.
Let me offer another analogy: the Sahā world is a vast ocean of karma, and the fish within that sea are exceedingly numerous.
"Many of you are fishermen who cast large nets into the sea to catch fish. When the net is full of fish and heavy, you are unable to drag it in;
instead, you are pulled back into the sea by the weight of the fish. If, while dragging the net, a man of great strength were to come and take over the main rope for you..."
I have dragged it up myself. The great ocean is like the triple world; the fish within the sea are like the good and evil karmic conditions you have encountered throughout successive lifetimes.
Your resolve to rescue others from all sufferings is like the net used to catch fish.

Being dragged into the sea by the fish is like mistakenly entering the paths of external teachings and becoming deluded by worldly conditions, ultimately sinking into the ocean of karma. A person of great strength assists in releasing [the fish].
The end of the rope is Amitābha Buddha. Amitābha Buddha was originally a fisherman who, throughout kalpas, employed great compassion and wisdom to rescue sentient beings from the ocean of karma.
You all must practice the recitation of the Buddha’s name with diligence to deliver those with whom you have emotional ties;
thus you shall benefit both yourselves and others. Without relying on the great power of Amitābha Buddha, you cannot be born upon the other shore. You!
If you do not call upon Amitābha, you will willingly sink into the depths and transmigrate through the three miserable realms.
Although Amitābha Buddha spreads his net to await the fish, if the fish do not enter the net, the fisherman can only sigh in regret. You all must quickly awaken!
Furthermore, there is another analogy: these three realms are called the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm; above, they reach the limit of existence...
From the Peak of Existence (*bhavāgra*) down to the Avīci Hell, beings are born within the three realms. Those born in the heavens fall back once their merit is exhausted;

those undergoing retribution return again once their punishment is finished. They revolve upward and downward without any prospect of escape, like a three-tiered steamer filled with buns and dumplings, placed daily over a cauldron of boiling water to be steamed.
On the lid of the steamer there is but a single small hole, through which one must reach to feel for the food.

What is this teaching? The first layer of the cage corresponds to those above the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, including the various celestial immortals (*deva-rṣi*), earth-dwelling immortals (*bhūmi-rṣi*), the ranks of the four dhyānas, and the sages.
The second layer of the cage corresponds to kings, lords, generals, ministers, and the common people, both rich and poor.
The third layer of the cage corresponds to the spirits and ghosts within the hells of the underworld. Above these is a single canopy, which encompasses all devas, immortals, humans, and animals.
They are unable to transcend the three realms. This refers precisely to the "three-layered steamed buns.
Within the three realms—among devas, humans, asuras, ghosts, and animals—beings revolve upward and downward without ceasing, like an overturned basket.

The single spiritual true nature of sentient beings is, from life to life and age to age, constantly subjected to steaming and baking; it becomes parched, withered, dark, and dim, utterly devoid of radiance. Consequently, they are unable to...
To emerge from the seven realms of transmigration is like being covered by a cage; yet there is one eye that can perceive it.

This is the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha, by which one transcends the three realms horizontally, is born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, enters the lotus womb, and attains great, pure coolness. I have set forth these three metaphors, all of which are extremely simple and profoundly true.

May you, my children, realize them with an impartial mind. When Jingfo asked Master Wuhui about his background, the Master replied that he was originally at the stage of Sublime Enlightenment (*miao-jue*).
An emanation body came from the East, entrusting himself to birth and leaving the household life to sustain this great kalpa.

Generally, whenever a Great Bodhisattva manifests in the world to propagate the Dharma and save sentient beings, they encounter many demonic afflictions. That they do not regard these as suffering is due to nothing other than their ability to realize the *pāramitā* of patience (*kṣānti*).
You have now met Master Wu; fortunately, the roots of your goodness are profound, making them easy to sprout and grow. Otherwise, you would have had to...
A face-to-face encounter has been missed. The great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions are ever-present in the world, yet those with worldly eyes are ignorant and have missed them many times.

Now that this altar is about to be dismantled, I bestow upon you all a dose of the wondrous medicine of coolness, to ensure that you may cast off your hands and return to the West, where you shall behold the Buddha as the flowers bloom.
As for the method: at every hour and every moment, take Amitābha Buddha as the pill, using [the name] as...
Refined by the fire of samādhi, it is sent down by the water that returns to the source through wisdom; naturally, all hundred ailments are eliminated.
This is the most efficacious method.

When the six supernatural powers are perfectly radiant, the fruit is finally realized; without going or coming, one sees the original truth. In a single thought of empty clarity, suffering is eliminated;

throughout the ten directions, coldness turns into warm spring. When the golden bell is struck and shattered, it is difficult to awaken others; when the wooden clapper hangs suspended in vain, few are saved.
Wait until the conditions and opportunities have matured, then cast away the straw sandals and depart from the dusty world. —Wu Yongqinglian.
I realize that this is indeed so. After the long rains have first cleared, the new year gradually begins to change. The passage of time in this Sahā world is as swift as this.
Having reached old age to cultivate the Way, yet not knowing the profound mysteries within it—can one not feel a sense of dread?

Can one not give rise to a spirit of courageous diligence? Among the disciples of the Dharma field, those whose merit is deep have already attained rebirth; as for those who have not yet attained rebirth...

Furthermore, another year has passed. Youth is easily turned into old age; once old, one is further ravaged by decay. If one does not apply oneself with diligence at this time, when will one ever do so?
When life suddenly comes to an end and one is brought before the Lord of Yama, the retribution is merciless.
At that moment, though one cries out to the earth and calls upon heaven, it will be too late for regret. Amitābha Buddha welcomes sentient beings across the sea of suffering; simply recite His name.

One immediately ascends to the sacred realm. What is most feared is doubt and lack of faith; the heart’s aspiration becomes hollow and floating, one's practice lacks constancy, and one begins with diligence but ends in indolence.
Indeed, if one possesses even a single thought of true sincerity, one will attain horizontal transcendence beyond the three realms.

If, however, one is lax and negligent, with heavy hindrances and a light mind, and one's own vow is not firm—how could there be any further wondrous Dharma to deliver you? A verse says: "Adorning the Wondrous Body."
I have realized the Tathāgata. The vast, boundless ocean of suffering is truly pitiable; I wish to ferry all across with the Dharma-ship. This body shall never again return to the East.
A single point of numinous awareness is obscured by deep defilements; one’s own nature is buried and stifled within the red dust of the mundane world.
This is not due to the heavy power and majesty of demonic forces, but simply because those who practice lack sharp faculties.
The ground is of pure gold, and the towers are made of jewels; one knows not how many tens of thousands of autumns have passed since their creation.

Celestial birds dwell in serene seclusion, ever in peaceful joy; the sounds of the Dharma ring out clearly, and few feel sorrow. Those who take birth upon the lotus flowers all possess the "blue eyes" of enlightenment; those whose robes are made of lotus leaves rarely see a white hair.
They partake at will of the meals provided by the celestial kitchen, roaming freely through the jeweled groves and precious abodes. This is my Lian-yan Hermitage.

Master Mingzhou also said: "In vain one speaks of the journey being hundreds of millions of miles distant; it is by relying on these four characters that one transcends the sands of dust. Throughout the six periods he preaches the Dharma ever beneath the tree;
as the Three Sages discourse upon the sutras, flowers fall in profusion. Fragment after fragment, the clear stream pours forth like gold and jade; tier upon tier, the jeweled pavilions are verdant."
Clouds shroud me; there is neither cold nor heat, nor is there affliction. At ease and according to my will, I listen to the Lotus Sūtra.
I, the monk Songyuan of the Huangwang Temple, am now reborn in the Pure Land.
The lotus flowers of the four lands and the fragrances of the four lands—within each land, one beholds the King of Compassion. Avalokiteśvara constantly calls the deluded to awakening;
Mahāsthāmaprāpta repeatedly urges on the fragrance of the lotus buds. Having attained the samādhi of carefree, drifting clouds, the pure and secluded nectar cools the single mind.
Indeed, karmic obstructions are entirely eliminated; surely, one’s name shall be proclaimed throughout the Fragrant Forest. My Temple of the Wealth God.
This is Seng Danyuan.

"A single movement of thought and I know it all; worldly entanglements are nothing but delusion. Ascending the jeweled pavilion through a thousand layers, treading upon the lotus pond of five colors."

The music played is pure and exquisite; when one’s merit is perfected, the state of Nirvana is attained without delay. With the *kāṣāya* robe always draped over the body, it is naturally suited for both spring and summer.
This is I, the Abbot Wenming of Wucheng Monastery.
A single golden lotus emerges from the realm of quiescent light; treading upon it, one snaps the fingers and arrives at the altar.

Adorned with boundless vistas of precious pavilions, the burning of agallochum and sandalwood yields an extraordinary fragrance. Those seated here are all accomplished gentlemen; the Buddha enshrined within the shrine is the Compassionate King.
My arrival at this place is full of elegance and ease; it resembles the pure and peaceful land of the Lotus Realm. This is my Hall of the Three Contemplations.
The Abbot Wǎngshēng was also a monk who dwelt in the vast and boundless sea of suffering;
yet through pure karma, he was able to escape it. Among ordinary monks, he was one who realized the fruits of enlightenment and attained the leisurely liberation of Sukhāvatī.
This was the Venerable Shùtián of the Dōngdǒu Altar.

The several monks mentioned above were all disciples who attained awakening under Master [Wu]. While practicing the recitation of the Buddha’s name at the Yongqing Monastery, they passed away and were reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss;
the judgment records are clear and distinct—how could these be mere false claims?
I have already attained a human body; I have emerged from this human existence. I have come forth from hell, and I shall enter into hell.
When I emerge, I serve the Buddhas; when I enter, I deliver sentient spirits. I deliver the souls of all beings; I am the Buddha of the Western Paradise.
I am Ni Xiu of the Guanyin Hermitage in Gaoyou; I am here following Master Wu to pay a visit with you all and reminisce about our long separation.

Time flows swiftly; in the blink of an eye, several years have passed. In my two previous lives, I received a female body and wandered again through the six realms and three miserable paths, willingly enduring suffering and affliction.
Now that those with whom I share a karmic affinity have been delivered and liberated, I shall return to the higher realms.

Chapter. Since you have already resolved to transcend the world, you should practice the Bodhisattva path, diligently cultivating the six perfections and the myriad deeds, enduring all sufferings, and exhausting all emotional attachments without giving rise to retreat or regret. You should apply yourself to your practice in the sea of suffering as soon as possible.
It is essential to cast aside all external affairs; why needlessly burden this finite body with useless worldly entanglements?
The sound of the Dharma flows unceasingly like the sands of the Ganges; having read the *Śūraṅgama*, one recites the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.

The hundred-and-eightfold silence of the Muni turns ever-present, while the birds’ songs resound naturally through the six periods of the day. Radiant jewel forests grow by the edge of the pond, and the fragrance of lotuses wafts from the water’s shore.
From this point on, I shall cast my straw sandals within the seas, accustomed to treading upon lotus flowers with both feet. I shall be reborn in the Ultimate Bliss.
This was the Bhikṣuṇī Benlian of Guanyin-an.
When the Master was born, she made a vow before the Buddha: "After my disciple passes away, I wish that this illusory body shall not decay, remaining here to exhort future students.

When the Master entered parinirvāṇa, she followed custom and performed cremation. Although the fire was maintained for a full day and night, the top of the sarcophagus had not yet scorched, nor had the corpse [decomposed].

It was merely stained black, yet not a single thread of it was damaged. The assembly prepared a reliquary shrine for its enshrinement. Master Wan, the Commander of the Water Armies, donated his personal funds and attire as gold.
This indestructible vajra-body shall thus remain eternally in this Sahā world. I record this here as a supplement.

All sentient beings have been moistened by blessings and wisdom. Amidst the precious lotuses of Ultimate Bliss, their merit and virtue are now fully perfected; this is entirely due to the power of mindfulness of the Buddha.
In two previous lifetimes, I was a monk who maintained the precepts at Longquan Temple; in the lifetime prior to that, I was a member of the Zhang clan in Gansu.
His official rank reached that of the Shaanxi Circuit. Upon being summoned to the capital for an audience, he encountered the Elder Wuhé at the monastery on Mount Hongluo.

They discussed the sutras for two days, whereupon his intellectual obstructions were suddenly cleared away and his aspiration to take refuge was born. The Elder bestowed upon him the name Jingguang. After practicing for three years, he resigned his office and returned to his hometown.
Every day he recited the Buddha’s name thirty thousand times and chanted ten scrolls of the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*. In the evening, he would...
My daily practice is to dedicate my merits before the Buddha. Each month, I release three thousand creatures and observe the fast for six days. I consume only the three kinds of pure meat.
At the age of sixty-one, I shall be reborn in the West, returning to the Land of Common Abode for the Ordinary and the Sages. This is I, Jingguang.
Old, old, old! Amidst the seven-jeweled ponds, the birds of suffering and emptiness cry out how many heroes there have been;

all have passed away like drifting clouds. Scattered white bones lie buried in the green grass—ah! Heaven is desolate and the world grows old. The realm of the Lotus Land is excellent; it is fitting to return early.
I, Han Tifu, belong to the lineage of Pure Wisdom (Jinghui). In the blink of an eye, it is the Duanwu Festival;
everywhere, hibiscus flowers vie with one another to bloom. Time passes as swiftly as a flying arrow; human life is but a theatrical stage.
This puppet-skin bag is but an ugly form; where can one find one's true home? My King Dunren Jingxiu—this is my Dharma name.

Only upon awakening to one’s original face does one truly know how to bring this floating life to an end. By the embankment, the willows are most heartless; they blow down falling blossoms until the path is strewn.
Were it not for the vastness of the Buddha-dharma, how could these drifting tufts ascend to the mat? One must firmly uphold the five...
He was a master of the precepts and a connoisseur of sounds. He had a fellow practitioner who lived nearby; he was Zhang Jinmen, whose Dharma name was Jingyuan.
Jinmen originally studied Confucianism, but later admired the arts of longevity and *daoyin* (guiding and pulling). He squandered his family fortune to extensively perform acts of merit.
He once lacquered a large gourd and personally prepared various medicinal compounds to place within it. During the summer, he carried it on his back...

A gourd hung from his shoulder; wearing straw sandals and a grass hat, he traveled through the countryside. Whenever he encountered a household, he would inquire, "Does your family have anyone who is ill?
If there was one, he would measure out a blade-tip of medicine according to the ailment, which invariably proved effective.
When the villagers saw him, they would joyfully exclaim, "Master Húlú has arrived! Dharma Master Wùhé marveled at this man, for he was skilled in aiding others.

Luan relied on his spiritual power to persuade the Master to invite the Buddha to descend upon the altar. Only then did Jinmen realize that while he had initially sought to solidify his physical form and refine his vital energy, he had ultimately fallen into emptiness and oblivion.
He subsequently reformed his practice by cultivating pure karma, awakening to the principle of non-arising. His faith and understanding surpassed those of his peers.
Hehe, here I come. From afar, I see a vast expanse of red light reaching up to the heavens. At first, I thought it was a fire;
however, I now know it to be the sound and light of those practicing the Buddha-remembrance (*buddhānusmṛti*), continuing on with the Great Compassionate Light of the Buddha.
How excellent, how excellent! I am Gao Jingshun. Your secular elder brother, the Dharma Master Wuhua.
A three-bay thatched cottage, leaning slightly to one side; this is my home, desolate and poor as it may be. On this day, the Lotus Land is most serene and sublime;
in years to come, I shall pass my life in quietude there. This is Chen Jingwu, who is destined for rebirth.
I have mingled my traces among men for sixty springs; through sorrows, joys, partings, and reunions, my spirit has been secretly wounded.
Today, having cultivated myself to the stage of the Lotus Pond, I finally attain carefree wandering and cast off the dust of the world. I am the reborn King of Purity, Po-ya.
Neither self nor person; the dust of worldly toil obscures the true nature. Once the mirror of the mind becomes clear, a lotus releases a branch of spring.
This is Qin Jingde.

This is originally the essence of purity and truth, yet it is obscured by the karmic hindrances of this Sahā world. When the flower blooms and the ground of the mind is purified, the Land of Ultimate Bliss is none other than one's own home.
I am that King of Pure Masters to whom you shall be reborn.

My five defiled bodies have become obstructed by much impurity; for the sake of sons and daughters, I labored in toil and haste. Only this morning have I recognized the illusions within the dust of the world;
now, with a smile, I shall cast forth emerald lotuses in the Lotus Land. This is Zhang Jingcheng, who is attaining rebirth there.
The bliss of rebirth in the West is beyond description; how easily could the "Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas" be spoken?
Casting off this illusory body, one returns to one's own nature, roaming at ease in the pure realm and enjoying security. I shall be reborn in the Pure Land of Amitābha.
Those who cultivate the mind-ground generally find it difficult to remain steadfast; they are all pulled by the fleeting interests and desires of this floating world.

Once one reaches the point where practice and realization are fully perfected, one will naturally become a solitary carp leaping toward the heavens. This is precisely what I mean by being reborn in the Pure Garden of Wei.
The vast ocean of suffering stretches boundlessly; for many years, all have been submerged in manifold afflictions. Fortunately, Amitābha has come to guide us;
from this moment, through the practice of the mind, we shall sit upon the golden lotus. I am Gaòng Jingzhì of the Wisdom Dharma-hall.
A single golden lotus contains a Buddha; all living beings are delivered as they tread upon the lotus flowers.
Their carefree and pure blessings rival those of the myriad immortals, yet they surpass the immortals by a hundredfold. This is none other than I, Zhu Jingkong.
Heavenly flowers fall in profusion like hemp seeds; the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss is my home. Sitting in silence, I recite the Buddha's name within my heart;
when inspiration arises, my feet tread upon lotus blossoms. This is the Dharma-assembly of wisdom by Qian Jingyuan.
Born in the West in Sukhāvatī to nourish one’s true nature; cast aside both the former life and the future body. After death, it is as if pouring hot water on snow;
yet one still hears companions speak of the red dust of the mundane world. This is the "Wangsheng Qian" (Money for Rebirth) from the Wisdom Dharma-hall of Wujie.
Pine winds blow; the midday dream returns. With eyes blurred from sleep, I awaken and go home. Where is the setting sun on the western mountain?
A single stroke of the bell resounds like thunder. This is my sanctuary of wisdom: Song Jingji.
A single lotus contains a single nature; when the mind is pure, the lotus is pure. If you wish to return to the West, maintain one-pointed concentration.
This is my wisdom *bodhimaṇḍa*, Lu Jingxiang.
Abiding in this world relies entirely upon meritorious deeds; departing for the world beyond relies entirely upon Father Amitābha.
If one can unify these two thoughts into a single thought, every step will be upon the golden bridge and the jade path. I, Zhao Jingheng, [say].

Throughout my life, I have most cherished the recitation of Amitābha’s name. Having lived in this world without cause, I suffered endless afflictions. On this day, I roam freely back to the Pure Land;
atop the Purple Gold Terrace, I lament the Saha World. I am Zhu Jingshi.
A lifetime of toil has brought me to white hair; fame, office, and wealth are but ephemeral mayflies. Today I have cast aside my thatched cottage;
let me roam freely through the pavilions of the seven treasures. All anxieties are empty, far removed from worldly dust; I shall be the first to ascend the Adorned Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Cease your attachment to this illusory body, like a floating bubble; I vow to take the highest tier of the Lotus Throne. I myself take refuge.

Master Wuda awakened to the truth that the past is entirely illusory and the future is utterly empty. Having realized the means for transcending the world, how could he dare to indulge in leisure or self-indulgence?
From then on, he diligently cultivated the pure karma, repenting of his former transgressions.

Relying entirely upon the single sound of Amitābha and firmly embracing the four characters of the True Mantra, he upheld the precepts with a settled mind and resolved upon authentic practice. He established a fixed daily regimen of recitation.

Beyond these moments, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, I was never apart from even a single phrase of Amitābha. Even during times of illness and suffering, I persevered in my recitation.
Thus, for three years, through the Buddha’s compassion, I was welcomed at the end of life and, reaching the age of sixty, attained realization in the Lotus Pond.
You, my fellow practitioners and descendants, should take me as your model and act accordingly.
Cultivate yourself in this manner so as to realize it; I have high expectations for you.
Written by Cheng Jingti (this was the hand of Zhao Luan’s father) from the Middle Grade Superior Birth in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.

Sentient beings of billions of kinds possess billions of dispositions; they drift through the ocean of suffering in all four directions. Why not die with the mind returning to a single thought-moment?
In an instant, one may attain liberation and realize the Lotus Land. This is my path of pure precepts. Before my birth, I took refuge in Master Wu;

before the Buddha, I gave rise to a heart of true faith, aspiration, and practice. I recited the Buddha’s name, maintained vegetarianism, released living beings, and abstained from killing. Every day...

Take one pinch of spirit-writing sand and one *liang* of incense ash; mix with vinegar and honey and apply it.
The efficacy will be like a shadow following a form or an echo responding to a sound; the punitive talisman shall be granted.
Seeking the essential methods requires a sincere heart; without sincerity, how can there be spiritual efficacy?
Use one and a half catties of high-quality incense and one catty of wax candles.
—From the *Lianxiu Qixìn Lù*, Scroll Five.
