by Cheng Zhao-luan of Hailing;
Preface on the Weariness with Mundane Turbidity.
Petition for the Emptiness of the Prisons:
A Petition for Taking Refuge in the Triple Gem by the Disciple of Pure Practice, [Name], who now bares his whole heart and bows his head in earnest supplication before the Ten [Directions].

Throughout the entirety of space, its atoms, and the Dharma-realm, I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the two lands of Śākyamuni and Amitābha, and the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who manifest through expedient means within the seven realms of existence.

Before these golden lotus seats, I represent all the lands as numerous as motes of dust and the three miserable paths where beings undergo immeasurable suffering. I beg for grace to have my transgressions pardoned and to be uplifted to transcend this life. Alas, I, your disciple, am filled with grief.
I take pity upon those within the seven realms of existence; among them, the sentient beings of the three miserable paths suffer double the torment.
Whether in the past, present, or future, there are those—whether their offenses be light or heavy—who shall not escape suffering for as many as a thousand billion kalpas.

This is all because while living their days, these sentient beings were greedily preoccupied with mere food and drink, slaughtering living creatures, committing adultery and seizing what is not theirs, harming human lives, and violating the precepts.

According to the celestial laws: to defile the divine spirits; to slander and destroy the Triple Gem; to draw blood from the body of a Buddha; to commit great treachery and great evil; to be unfilial and disloyal;
to obstruct others from leaving the household life; and to commit the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes—such deluded and inverted actions accumulate karma that is profoundly heavy.
Deluded in my true mind, I was ignorant of repentance; consequently, the winds of karma buffeted me, and the rākṣasas stood in solemn array.

Three times each day, my body underwent the punishments of the underworld. Only now do I have some awareness, yet there is no door through which I may seek salvation. This soul receives its retribution because its transgressions were self-incurred.
Yet, the Buddha-nature is one and the same as our own nature; the minds of others and myself are one. When another falls into the realms of suffering, how is it different from my own experience?
The disciple reflects upon this again and again; his heart truly finds it difficult to endure. Desiring to bring about their salvation, he finds his strength feeble and his form insignificant.
Now, he entreats all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with deep sorrow: may you deign to look down upon this disciple’s foolish sincerity and expand your vast and great compassion for saving sentient beings.
Through the power of your great compassionate vows, manifest the light of great majesty, so that the suffering of sentient beings in the three miserable realms may be brought to an end.

Those who flee [from their transgressions] shall, by this standard, transcend rebirth through minor offenses. Those whose offenses may be pardoned shall follow the disciples in reciting the Buddha’s name and taking refuge, thereby escaping the suffering of the kalpas.

The karmic retribution for slandering the sages shall be eliminated; the evil karma of killing and lust shall be dissolved. Thus realizing the true, one shatters the false; with a mind free of artifice, one becomes pure.
With no dharmas remaining, one leaves behind all dust. One is liberated from the root of birth and death, and proceeds unhindered toward the Radiance.
Treading upon lotus flowers, their divine majesty is immeasurable. Without passing through the four modes of birth, all nine grades ascend [to liberation].
Those ground by pestles or sawn asunder all rely upon the compassionate clouds of radiant wisdom; those who consume iron or swallow copper are instantly transformed into the nectar of cool serenity.

Rivers of enmity and oceans of resentment are entirely transformed into lotus ponds; barrier ridges and encircling mountains all become lands of jewels. Lamentations of grief turn into liberation, and darkness...

The self-nature of darkness is inherently luminous. Regardless of this land or other lands, this world or other worlds, throughout immeasurable and inexhaustible realms—may all solitary spirits who are submerged in the bitter torments of the three miserable paths rely entirely upon the Buddha’s grace to be fully delivered.
This humble disciple only prays that the Buddha’s arm may ever be extended, compassionately leading them into the fragrant grove, again and again.

Having received this transcendent deliverance, may all who have followed in succession ascend to the Pure Realm and share in eternal safety. Through the sincerity of these repentances, may those remaining be extracted from suffering;
through universal salvation in every season, may those left behind be uplifted toward rebirth. May each of the hells become empty and luminous, and may all together ascend to Wondrous Enlightenment.
We beg for Your gracious consideration and approval; our gratitude shall be boundless. Respectfully submitted.

Bestowing elixirs to save living beings is preeminently the work of bestowing elixirs to save living beings. I humbly consider that although the nature of light is inherently present in all wriggling and crawling creatures, those born from wombs, eggs, moisture, or transformation find it difficult to partake of the flavor of the Dharma.
We, the disciples, embodying the Buddha’s sacred compassion and generating the power of sincere mindfulness, [offer] this divine elixir...
It is scattered everywhere; nectar is bestowed upon all. Relying on the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, boundless beings are universally saved.

Rivers, lakes, streams, and oceans—no single drop of water is left out. Fields, roads, mountains, and forests—no place remains unserved. As soon as it enters the mouths of living beings, they immediately realize the nature of their karmic retribution.
All Buddhas maintain a heart of rescue and protection; throughout ten thousand kalpas, they plant the seeds of compassion, ensuring that none shall suffer at the butcher’s knife or cutting board.
Forever liberated from the cage; thoroughly understood, thoroughly understood. There is no need for retribution in a future life. Emptiness, emptiness, emptiness, emptiness.

Without waiting to be slaughtered, one dies of oneself. Relying upon this single speck of dust and a single drop of water, one delivers and liberates the infinite. One must know that the illusory is itself the real.
Transcending birth shall no longer cease; the winds and waves of the ocean of karma are suddenly stilled. All may board the precious raft, and the merits of the Fragrant Forest are boundless.
May the lotus chambers of Sukhāvatī be reached through sincere devotion. Realizing that life is cherished, one knows the source of the establishment of destiny;
proceeding westward in succession, one saves living beings and realizes the realm of non-birth. Having offended Your compassionate countenance, I beg for Your grace and permission.
A Petition for the Dispelling of Calamities and Misfortunes.
This petition is made for the purpose of dispelling disasters and perils. I humbly observe that violent winds and excessive rains are summoned by karmic retribution;

spring epidemics and autumn plagues are stirred by the human heart itself. Through the ritual of repentance, the root of sinful karma is fundamentally emptied; through the practice of repentance, the entanglements of resentment are entirely transformed. I pray—
The Buddhas do not violate their original vows nor abandon their great compassion. They emit the light of great wisdom, the light of great peace and bliss, and the light of great auspiciousness.
They gather and subdue the pestilential spirits and ghosts, causing them to come to this *bodhimaṇḍa* to listen to the sutra and recollect the Buddha.

By borrowing the sound and light of the recollection of the Buddha, their anger and rage are dissolved, their calamities and misfortunes are dispelled, their burning afflictions are entirely transformed into coolness, and their poisonous hatred is converted.
Joyful and benevolent, may all karmic defilements be purified and all calamities naturally eliminated. I universally pray that all those in distress may be spared from misfortune;

through faith and aspiration, may they hold the Name with increasing firmness, attaining single-mindedness without distraction and swiftly achieving samādhi. I humbly beseech your compassion to take pity on us and grant this request.

To be rescued from drowning and emerge preeminent after being submerged for kalpas is a matter of petitioning for grace to be uplifted from this plight. I humbly observe that rivers, lakes, streams, and seas are all perilous paths;

for those traveling as sojourners, it may be difficult to cross their borders. When winds rage and waves surge, lives are lost and bodies overturned. Furthermore, there are those who are burdened by accumulated grief.

In a fit of rage, he drowned himself in a deep abyss; encountering his enemies, he threw himself into the water, thereby causing his vengeful spirit to remain trapped in the underworld, seeking retribution without end.

Reflecting upon this, I feel profound sorrow and compassion. Now, I, your disciple, respectfully establish this *dharmāśraya* (Dharma-hall) for [number] days, relying upon the great compassionate power and the majestic radiant light of all Buddhas.
Regardless of whether they reside in this world or other worlds, all who are...
The souls of those who have drowned in rivers, lakes, seas, mountain streams, brooks, harbors, canals, wells, springs, and ponds, having received this light, may they attain deliverance;

through mindfulness of the Buddha, may they transcend this life, resolve their grievances and enmities, and no longer harbor thoughts of retribution, as they look up to receive the compassionate radiance. We humbly entreat you to grant us your permission.
Transcending his ancestors and standing out as a preeminent example, he established this rite of repentance for the sake of repaying kindness.

To universally plant the causes for rebirth in the Lotus Land—this is truly the profound compassion with which our Buddha has enlightened and exhorted me, a disciple who has fortunately obtained a human body, been born in Zhendan (China), heard the True Dharma, and encountered pure conditions; it shall endure for a thousand ages.

Upon encountering this opportune moment, I reflect only on where my own body has come from and where its debt of gratitude begins. Tracing it back to its single source, it is boundless and difficult to fathom.
For kalpa after kalpa, I, your disciple, have been mired in delusion and have not known how to repay [this kindness].

Consequently, the parents of many lifetimes still linger on the dark path, and the ancestors through successive eons have not yet reached the other shore. I reproach myself for my stupidity and obstinacy, as my transgressions have increased ever more. Now...

This disciple prostrates himself at the Gate of Compassionate Grace, looking upward in prayer for deliverance. Though his heart is courageous, his strength is timid; he hopes that through spiritual resonance, this path may be opened.

Now, having gathered various fellow practitioners of the Way, he reverently establishes a Universal Buddha Altar for several days, respectfully reciting several fascicles of Mahāyāna sūtras and universally bestowing the Dharma-food of ambrosia.
He entreats with deep sorrow all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions to take pity upon this disciple.
This is the humble sincerity of your disciple. May you, having surveyed my subtle vow to deliver sentient beings, bestow great majestic power and radiate great light,
so that the soul-consciousnesses of the parents and ancestors of this disciple from beginningless time until now—
and likewise the parents and ancestors of each and every generation throughout all lifetimes, including their respective soul-consciousnesses— may reach one another through their shared emotions.
Sentiments are infinite; as one condition meets another, these conditions push forward inexhaustibly.

Such immeasurable, boundless, and unspeakable emotional conditions, scattered among the sentient beings of the seven realms throughout the ten directions, all rely upon the majestic radiance of the Triple Gem to be gathered and brought to this site of practice.
There, they hear the sutras and mindfulness of the Buddha, whereby their attachments are suddenly transformed and the ground of their minds becomes clear. Thus they perform repentance.

Repenting of former transgressions, the multitudes return to the Land of Ultimate Bliss; boundless suffering and affliction are instantly transformed into lotus ponds, and all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm together realize the Wisdom of All Modes.
Respectfully submitted.

To pull back the kalpa and manifest this as a means for repenting of transgressions is a matter of great significance. I humbly consider that the nature of sin is fundamentally empty and the creation of karma is likewise illusory;

yet, because the mind fails to realize this, illusions provoke illusions and one undergoes illusions. All manner of illusory miseries are arrayed before our eyes. Once the act of creation has become habitual, the retribution will likewise be fierce.
Severe! The karma of the mountain-affairs has been created; I repent so that these affairs may be removed. Within that which is beyond repentance, I seek repentance;

within that which is beyond recovery, I seek recovery. Now, for the sake of all sentient beings of this great earth, I bitterly repent before the Triple Gem, so that they may know the Triple Gem is worthy of reverence and faith, and so that they may know the Triple Gem is [the refuge] of all sentient beings of this great earth.

True refuge for body, speech, and mind, you bring gentleness and compliance to the three karmas. You cause all those who have committed the five heinous crimes, the ten evil acts, or violated the fundamental social norms—those of every kind of grave offense—to be awakened and to repent until they are purified.
By the power of reciting the Buddha’s name, you universally permeate all sentient beings.
May each and every consciousness be swiftly matured and swiftly liberated. Relying upon the wondrous power of the *dhāraṇī*, may the retribution of sins be extinguished like flowers in the sky.
Once the eons of destruction have ended, may those sentient beings assist in propagating the True Dharma and together return to the Pure Land. Respectfully submitted.
Verse: A Verse for Assisting in Mindfulness at the Hour of Death (Spoken by Elder Wuhé; Verses composed by Zhàoluán).

Disciple [Name]: Since beginningless time, through the power of delusion, karma, and perversion, I have repeatedly ascended and descended among the various realms of existence. My debt of gratitude...

How can enmity ever reach its end? Because of the power of binding together both kindness and resentment, the demands for retribution have no bottom or limit. Only the Great Hero of the World has pointed the way back to the world of Sukhāvatī.
I have already made the great vow to rescue and deliver beings without ceasing until the very end of time. I entreat all you who have been kind or hostile: wait for me as I go to be reborn there.
Once I have been reborn there, my oath shall certainly not be in vain; I shall constantly turn the Wheel of Dharma, [bringing relief] to those in extreme suffering.
One will certainly attain salvation from suffering. Now, before the Three Jewels, I swear that there is not the slightest deception in my vow.
May all the Buddhas and Amitābha bear witness to this pledged vow.
Master Wuhé said: "When a practitioner reaches the end of life, they rely entirely upon the mind-king not abandoning them; with a single thought directed straight [toward the Pure Land]..."

[Zhao] said: "However, this is not the case for those who have not cultivated earnest and practical effort during their daily lives, remaining single-mindedly without distraction. When the moment arrives, their consciousness is scattered and their spirits are clouded;
unable to maintain self-mastery, the karmic obstacles of many lifetimes manifest before them, and they are led away by these enticements.

Among my disciples throughout the Jiangnan region, numbering in the tens of thousands, those with sharp faculties are very few. They do not seek diligent progress, and even when the sprouts of goodness occasionally emerge, they say:"

Once long withered and dried up, it will be of no use whatsoever at the time of death. Therefore, know that even for rebirth while carrying one's karma, one must rely on the causal conditions as a guide.
I now leave behind this verse. You all should habitually recite the name of the Buddha until you have completed one chart;
if possible, forty-eight million times, or otherwise, four million eight hundred thousand times. Up to...
It is forty-eight thousand fewer [than the full number]. The text was written with blood and is enshrined before the Buddha in the monastery for offerings.

Should one’s consciousness become clouded at the time of death, one should immediately present this image and the memorial tablet, instructing one’s children to reverently incinerate them before the Buddha.
Furthermore, request five or six people to recite the Buddha’s name by the bedside; through this assistance in recitation, the deceased’s mental faculty—
When they regain consciousness, they may then embrace the Buddha and depart for the West. After their breath has ceased, do not move the body.
Continue to recite the Buddha’s name aloud for two incense sticks. Then dress the deceased and prepare them for burial.

For a person, the single point of true spirit arrives first when entering a womb and departs last after the body has grown cold. At that time, one must strictly avoid wailing, which stirs up worldly thoughts; once such worldly thoughts arise—
If there is movement [of the mind], rebirth will be difficult. This is specifically intended for those whose practice has not yet reached purity.

If one possesses genuine power and genuine realization, one can naturally maintain mastery and need not rely on this method. Furthermore, if the parents or elders-in-law do not personally prick their own blood, [the ritual cannot proceed].
It is also permissible for those of lower station to recite and chant on one’s behalf; this is done out of filial piety.
This verse for burning at the stupa is offered in refuge to the Triple Gem. Disciple Upāsaka, whose Dharma name is Shijingfo (Isingbuddha), with utmost sincerity and profound reverence.
I prostrate my head and bow again, writing this vow with blood drawn from my own veins. I entreat the ten directions throughout the inexhaustible realm of empty space:
may the Sahā world become equal to the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Before the golden lotus thrones of the holy sages of both lands and the assembly of all bodhisattvas, I offer this prayer.
Among the heavy kindnesses in the world, none is greater than that of one's parents; next is that of one's teachers and elders.
Since the time I emerged from the womb, my parents have nurtured me; as I gradually grew into adulthood, my teachers and elders have instructed me. From beginningless time...

Throughout kalpa after kalpa, beings have been deluded and inverted; their parents and teachers have long remained submerged within the seven realms of existence, with no means to escape from all sufferings.
Whether born from a womb, an egg, moisture, or by transformation, it is likewise for all: those who have given birth to me have all been my parents.

Extending this further and broadening its scope: among those who have been each other’s parents, the evil karma created therein is immeasurable and boundless, while the wholesome fruits cultivated therein are as minute as a single mustard seed. Within that interval of good and evil, various kinsmen are formed.

Parents and teachers, relatives and friends—whether one has mistakenly injured them or consumed their flesh, or whether they have been creditors or enemies—throughout kalpa after kalpa in every world, one undergoes the suffering of rising and sinking among the seven realms of existence. Retribution follows retribution in a cycle that knows no end.
I have long gazed in hope for salvation, yet had no means to escape these various sufferings. Now, fortunately, I have obtained a human body and been born within the Middle Kingdom.

During the Xianfeng era of the Great Qing, I further encountered an enlightened master who provided instruction and pointed out the path through the mists; only then did I come to know the practice of the Pure Land.
If one knows that gratitude is not repaid, how can the heart endure it? One should give rise to a heart of compassion, just as the Buddha delivers all from suffering.
Yet, currently fallen into the stage of an ordinary person, one’s karmic offenses are deep and heavy; though one may resolve upon this supreme mind, one’s strength is too feeble to provide salvation.
Now, before the Three Jewels, I light eight hundred incense sticks on behalf of all sentient beings who have been mutual benefactors or enemies.
I offer them to the Honored Buddhas throughout the inexhaustible realm of empty space. Having made this universal offering, I earnestly entreat you to accept it.
Having already accepted [the teachings], may I and all sentient beings, among the entire multitude of living beings, each exhaust the defilements of our respective karma.
Having performed the ritual of reverent prostration, confession, and aspiration for three days, we shall cremate the Glorious Stūpa and make offerings to the Sūtra written in blood.
The thirty-two sections of the *Gongbu* (Common Section), including the treatises of the Patriarchs, totaling eighteen volumes, have been completed.

To the Buddhas of the past and the future, and to all the holy ones upon their lotus seats, I offer these seven tiers of stupas in gratitude for my upbringing and nurture. I rely upon the majestic power of all the Buddhas.
The Universal Radiance Victorious Stūpa, through its spiritual power, encompasses all of space;

it shines upward as far as the Peak of Existence and downward to the five Avīci hells, radiating horizontally throughout the ten directions—boundless and limitless—throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, including the four intermediate points, above, and below.
A great radiance shines everywhere; all rely upon the majestic spiritual power of the Buddhas to be thus. Amidst this, sentient beings hear the sutra and attain liberation;
beholding the light, their karmic defilements are purified. Universally they give rise to faith, aspiration, and practice, each determined to be born [in the Pure Land].
From this, I shall escape the cage and proceed together toward the Western Land.

By the sacred grace of all Buddhas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas, may you descend upon this site of practice upon lotus flowers and act as my witnesses and guarantors; hear me recite my vow. I now give rise to this great aspiration.

I have pricked my own blood to transcribe the Honored Sūtras and the Mahāyāna treatises of the Patriarchs. Above, I repay the fourfold heavy debts of gratitude; below, I rescue those suffering in the three miserable realms.
Throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—whether sentient or non-sentient, whether possessing a karmic connection or not—in every single ocean of Buddha-lands:

Throughout the ocean of sentient beings in the realms of earth, among all the paths of the seven destinies, those who have mutual emotional affinities—should anyone see or hear them, may they all resolve upon the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta).
There is no difference between these thorns and those written characters; they universally perfume the seeds within all consciousnesses.
There shall not be one who is left behind; once they have all attained Buddhahood, I shall then realize wondrous enlightenment.

I will adorn a single jeweled stupa and offer it throughout the entirety of space, continuing until the end of the future. In every land, during both the True and Semblance Dharma periods, I will manifest my body to guide and receive them.

The precious stupa swiftly appears before them; its light radiates throughout the ten directions—boundless and limitless. This light shines upon all sentient beings and all those with whom they share a karmic connection.
For those sentient beings who have sunk into suffering due to various uninterrupted karmic offenses, the light shines and they immediately resolve their minds [upon awakening].

Having been illumined by the light of past karmic seeds, upon hearing this, they immediately experience profound joy. Whether through gradual or sudden maturation and liberation, and whether as individuals of the secret or indeterminate capacities, they all universally give rise to faith, aspiration, and practice;
each shall certainly attain rebirth. Reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing, each shall perfect the attainment of the Wisdom of All Modes.
May the Three Jewels throughout the entire Dharma-realm bear witness to my long-held aspiration. Furthermore, from the light of this jeweled stupa, immeasurable sounds emerge;
these sounds proclaim the contents of this stupa’s casket—the words and phrases of the sutra—and as the sounds resound with clarity, each person awakens to their own mind.

The mind awakens and swiftly attains realization; each reaches the wondrous enlightenment with speed. The scriptures of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are subtle; the Dharma-milk of the Patriarchs is true.

Whether horizontal or vertical, the principle of relative opposition increases spontaneously once it is transcended. Once that which is beyond opposition has increased, the feelings of joy and aversion become naturally more acute.
With a fervent sense of joy and renunciation, I shall certainly be born in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing.

By dedicating the merit of this writing to all sentient beings, may they each see the Buddha before the lotuses bloom and realize non-arising. Whether manifesting or remaining hidden, may he appear in various forms according to the capacities of each being.
Within this Lotus Pond of Deliverance, I vow that for all sentient beings, until the end of the future, until the realm of empty space is exhausted, until the realm of sentient beings is exhausted,
until the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and until the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, I shall remain within this immeasurable light of my precious stupa.
Immeasurable sounds pervade immeasurable Buddha-fields, continuing forever without end.
A Brief Account of the Transmission of the Dharma Master Heshang by Zhuanwuhe.
The Master’s Dharma name was Ruian; his secular surname was Gao, and he was a native of the capital. Having been ill since childhood, his parents made a vow for him to renounce the world.
At the age of nine, he received the tonsure at Mili Temple and was conferred the full precepts (*upasampadā*).

He planted his staff at the monastery on Hongluo Mountain, where he devoted himself exclusively to the practice of the Pure Land, reciting the Buddha’s name tens of thousands of times daily. Later, he vowed to journey to the sea and took up residence at a great monastery in Hangzhou, remaining there in silence.
Shen Wei-gong Yuan was the Prefectural Governor of Gaoyou. While serving in the central government offices, he followed a master to inquire about the Dharma.

After Wei had been appointed as a provincial governor and had been separated from his teacher for some time, his eldest son happened to be traveling to Zhejiang. There he encountered the Master at a temple and earnestly invited him to Gaoyou. The Governor was overjoyed;

he subsequently purified his guest quarters to serve as a quiet chamber for meditation. He visited the Master morning and evening to seek instruction in the Way. The Master, however, was a recluse of the mountains and forests and...
He took pleasure in residing at the prefectural office. When he requested to leave for a second time, the Prefect, noting that the Master’s conduct was preeminent, petitioned him to remain.

Fearing that the Master might still depart, the Prefect visited an ancient monastery within the district; once its repairs were completed, he sent his son and a member of his staff to accompany the Master on foot into the temple.
Only then did the Master come to understand the Prefect’s earnest desire to retain him. Realizing he could not decline, the Master consented.

He then resided there. Throughout his life, the Master devoted himself exclusively to pure cultivation; he performed prostrations and recitations during the six periods of the day and remained in the lotus posture all day long.
When travelers came to the temple to gaze upon him, he did not engage in the formalities of welcoming or seeing them off, and everyone praised him.

At that time, the "Hair-Band" rebels reached Shaobo, the "Twisted-Hair" bandits attacked Baoying, and the "Xue" rebels occupied the west of the lake. As the post station lay on a major thoroughfare, it was in imminent danger. (Zhao Luan) was at that time following [the Master].

The Master was traveling. One day, he encountered eight or nine fellow practitioners who came to visit him. When the conversation turned to the calamities of the times, the Master shed tears and said, "The karmic burden of killing among sentient beings is like a mountain;
their current lives are being repaid in full. None of this is anything other than the retribution for karma from previous births.

It is only that ordinary people have not yet realized the supernormal power of knowing past lives that they remain unaware of it themselves. My children, if you give rise to the Bodhicitta, even though great kalpas may be difficult..."
[The Master] withdrew. "This small corner of the world may remain safe and unharmed," he said. The assembly knelt and begged for his compassion.

Thereupon, the Master pricked his finger and shed blood, writing a memorial which he incinerated before the Buddha. He also burned one hundred sticks of arm-incense; we, too, each burned arm-incense, all for the sake of repenting the karma of the people of Yang-gun.
Furthermore, he addressed the assembly to form a ritual altar and recite the Buddha’s name for seven days and nights, chanting [the scriptures].
The scripture consists of three hundred fascicles. On the day of the formal repentance ceremony, more than two hundred people, both monastics and laypeople, gathered.

The Master donned his dharma robes and paid homage to the Buddha with profound sincerity, offering earnest prayers. He used willow-branch water to sprinkle everywhere—above, below, and in the four cardinal directions—and circumambulated while reciting the Great Compassion Mantra one hundred and eight times.
Leading the assembly, he walked around the courtyard chanting the Buddha’s name until dawn before the rite was concluded. Subsequently, the bandits indeed arrived.

He built an embankment and withdrew [the waters], whereby the people were brought to peace. Those who took refuge as disciples increased daily. The Master expanded three bays of the western corridor of the temple to establish a Lotus Society (*liánshè*).

On each of the six days of fasting, he led the assembly to the society and fixed their spiritual exercises: in the forenoon, they recited the Buddha’s name for six incense-burners and chanted six scrolls of scripture;
in the afternoon, he transmitted the *Yōumíng* (Mysterious Darkness) Precepts, and delivered a lecture on the sutras for half an incense-burner; in the evening...

He made it his constant practice to offer *amṛta* (sweet dew) and ritual meals. In the spring of the Bingchen year, Huang Kaibang, the Commander of the Navy, was stationed at Huxi and requisitioned the eastern corridor of the temple as a cannon foundry.
As military officials came and went, they peered into the master’s quarters; the Master sat in meditative posture (*paryaṅka*) and did not attend to them.
Huang Kaibang’s subordinates were angered by his haughtiness and reported the matter to him. The lecturer [thereupon] informed the Commander.

He deluded the masses, and those who relied upon him were many; it was feared he would become a great source of calamity. One day, when the official proclamation arrived, it coincided with the date of a local community festival.

Several hundred disciples had assembled, and when they saw the proclamation, they were startled and said, "The previous reports were not false. In a state of panic, they ordered soldiers to drag the Master down from his seat.
He bound the thumbs of both hands with a hempen rope and suspended them from a beam. That night, in a dream, countless people came before him begging for their lives.
In the midst of his extreme distress, a tall monk appeared and drove the crowd away. The man prostrated himself in gratitude;
suddenly, he awoke. The next day, when the man went to the office, he examined the master’s face and stature closely, and found they were identical to those seen in the dream.

The monks were undisturbed. [Yunju] ordered his bonds to be loosened and helped him into the master’s chamber. The master’s ten fingers were covered in congealed blood, and the swelling had increased tenfold;
for four days and nights he could not rise. After half a month, Yunju came again with the tally. He went straight into the chamber, where the master sat cross-legged reading a sutra without moving.

Later, when Fang Xiaoru’s father was preparing for his burial, he dreamed of an old man in vermilion robes who bowed to him and said: "The grave site you have chosen is near my dwelling.
I beg you to grant me three days' grace, waiting until my descendants have all moved away. Then I shall repay your kindness. Having spoken, he bowed again and again.
He prostrated himself. His father awoke, yet did not believe him; he opened the pit and saw several hundred red snakes, which he burned entirely.

Again, he dreamed of an old man weeping and saying: "I have already entreated you with the utmost sincerity and compassion; why then do you cause my eight hundred descendants to be consigned to a single flame?
Since you lack mercy, I shall also plot revenge. Later, Xu Xiaoru was born, who provoked the wrath of the Emperor Chengzu.

The ten clans were exterminated; those killed were as numerous as snakes. The Brahmajāla Sūtra states: "When a son of the Buddha sees beings of different species, he should give rise to the bodhicitta.
The Śūraṅgama Sūtra states: "As for the retribution for the karma of killing, even if it passes through kalpas as numerous as dust motes, they will continue to devour one another."
Life must be repaid, revolving like a wheel, with one taking the place of another in alternating rise and fall.

The *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states that the retribution for the karma of killing causes sentient beings to fall into the three miserable realms. The sūtra further says: "When sentient beings commit the karma of killing, they fall into the realm of animals."
There are two types. Those of heavy karma constitute determinate acts of killing, such as cattle, horses, pigs, sheep, chickens, and ducks.
Those of light karma constitute indeterminate acts of killing, such as the birds and beasts of the mountains and forests.

Furthermore, as one cycles through the six realms of existence, changing heads and faces, who knows that among the animal realm there may not be one's own kinsmen? This was once the case with Hanshan and Shide.
One day, as he was traveling alone, he saw a man riding a donkey by the side of the road. The donkey would not move forward, so the rider lashed it with a whip.
The two Great Beings sighed in lamentation. A fellow traveler asked them about this, and the Master said, "This donkey was the rider’s father three lifetimes ago.
By extension, how can one not refrain from killing? I exhort all people of the world: when you see another slaughtering an animal, give rise to the thought of saving and delivering it."

One should cultivate the thought of compassion; the thought of suffering; the thought of joy upon seeing others release living beings; the thought of liberation from hardship; and the thought of praise. As the Great Being Avalokiteśvara once said:
"When ordinary people engage in worldly activities, they primarily focus on two paths: those of form and taste.

Regarding the path of form, even those who possess a slight degree of self-love know to exercise restraint and caution. Yet, as for the mouth’s pursuit of flavors, they indulge their cravings and regard the act of slaughter as..."

Childish play. The world flows on in its current; long-standing habits are difficult to reverse. In this world, among wealthy families, it is not only livestock that have been slaughtered in great numbers;
they further use fish, shrimp, and other such creatures as soup ingredients, destroying eggs and embryos by the hundreds of millions at every turn.
As the Sūtra says: "If fish eggs are not treated with salt, they may still live after three years. Formerly, during the Xuānhuá era, there was a wealthy merchant...
Yang Xù wrote these words in large characters on a main thoroughfare. Seeing people buying fish, he urged them to throw them back into the river;

he also provided funds to search for and collect fish eggs. Later, a deity appeared in a dream and told him: "Your life was originally destined to end prematurely, but by saving these lives, you have preserved more than hundreds of millions of beings.
Your own lifespan may now be extended. Indeed, he lived to the age of ninety-eight and passed away without illness.
In the past, during the time of the Buddha, there was an arhat who brought blessings to sentient beings through his gradual teachings.
He encountered a woman named Guangmu (Light-Eye) who provided him with food as an offering. The arhat asked her, "What do you wish for?
Guangmu replied, "On the day my mother passed away, I sought to provide merit for her rescue and deliverance; I do not yet know in which realm she has been reborn. The arhat took pity on her.
To enter into meditative observation, he saw that this mother of Guangmu had fallen into the evil realms and was undergoing great suffering.
The Arhat questioned her: "What karmic actions did your mother perform while alive, that she now resides in the evil realms? Having heard this, Guangmu replied with sorrow:
"The habits my mother practiced were solely a fondness for eating fish, turtles, and other such creatures; she consumed many of these fish and turtles."
The number of his children would be ten million times that amount. O Venerable One, out of your compassion, how might you pity and rescue him?
Looking at it this way, the tasting of a single morsel of meat results in retribution for many kalpas; there is no escaping it. I urge all people of the world accordingly.

Even if you are unable to observe the precept against killing, whenever you encounter fish eggs, you must release them into the river. Over time, as these instances accumulate, this becomes a most effective method. The Buddha said:
"In every thought-moment one practices benevolence and compassion, one creates the body of a deva or human endowed with merit and virtue;

in every thought-moment one harms living beings and takes their lives, one creates the body of a hell-being or an animal. As for the way to protect life, maintain this intention wherever you are; do not disregard even the smallest good.
Do not do it. Do not think that because evil is small, one need not be cautious. From the small it reaches the great;
by extending this principle from things to people, one will naturally be suffused with wholesome energy, and the Great Harmony will flow everywhere in abundance.
In the "Zhongni" chapter of the *Liezi*, it quotes the words of Confucius: "I have heard that in the West there is a Great Sage who does not govern, yet the people are not disordered;
he does not speak, yet the people trust him; he does not transform them, yet the people act spontaneously.
Vast and boundless, the people are unable to give him a name. At that time, the Tripitaka and the twelve divisions of the scriptures had not yet arrived in the Eastern Land. Confucius...
They were unable to hear his teachings; thus, the two schools of Confucianism and Buddhism have often become like water and fire.
How could they know that our Śākyamuni Tathāgata, out of compassion for the sentient beings of the final age, descended from Tuṣita Heaven to be born in Central India?

He manifested as a prince who left the household life, practiced austerities, and attained the Way, becoming the Teacher of the Sahā World and the compassionate father of all sentient beings, succeeding the seven Buddhas.
This is the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the Sage among Sages, the God among Gods. There is none greater than the Buddha; there is none more venerable than the Buddha.
The source of the mind of the Three Teachings is clearly understood only by the Buddha. All myriad phenomena are born from the Buddha.

Even the most refined works of Confucianism may serve as a preliminary guide to the Buddha-dharma. All dharmas, both mundane and supramundane, do not lie outside the Buddha-dharma. How could this be...?

How could they even attempt to conjecture half a word [of its meaning]? Confucian scholars of the world are bound by the limited views gained from within a window; they have never even glimpsed the *palm-leaf* manuscripts.
Because they perceive the monastic discipline (*vinaya*) and the monastic precepts (*śīla*) as being different from worldly laws, they utter grand and deluded claims, branding them as heterodox.

Yet, when one examines what they actually study, it is nothing more than literary rhetoric and the arts of law and administration. They possess no understanding of the Sage’s fountainhead of mind or the lineage of the Way.
This is indeed a barrier. Examining their conduct, it does not go beyond startling the ignorant and adorning their own wit, indulging in the reckless abandonment of the physical frame;

it has no connection whatsoever with the bequeathed words and past instructions of our former masters. Yet, throughout successive dynasties, many renowned figures of the School of Principle (Lixue) were well-versed in the teachings of Buddhism.

Frequently, through this, one awakens to the profound source of the mind. A sutra states: "Within the four great continents, there are nineteen hundred countries where the scriptural texts of the Bequeathed Teachings on palm leaves have been obtained;
as for the remaining lands, the merit of their sentient beings is meager, and they are unable to hear the teachings."

The Buddha-Dharma abides in the world; to encounter it is exceedingly difficult. That you have fortunately met with the True Dharma is because, throughout many lifetimes, you have made offerings to the Buddhas and planted roots of goodness.
If you do not take advantage of this auspicious light to resolutely reform your past errors and strive with bitter determination to discern the Way, [you will miss this opportunity].
I fear that once one loses this human body, it will be difficult to regain for ten thousand kalpas.
Among those in the world who seek the Way, some practice meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), while others steadfastly cultivate breath-regulation (*ānāpāna*).

They hope to attain the Way, ascend to the heavens, and achieve eternal life without death. In the minds of such people, they consider the pursuit of immortals to be the ultimate limit of practicing the Way.

How could one know that the cultivation of the path of the immortals (*ṛṣi*) is difficult to accomplish through arduous toil? Even if one should fortunately attain immortality, when merit is exhausted, one cannot avoid falling back.

As the Sūtra says: "Those with past virtue have their retributive merit manifest before them and can be reborn in the heavenly realms; yet when the merit of celestial immortals is exhausted, they fall."

Those with residual karma encounter the manifestation of evil retributions and further fall into the three miserable realms. When the karmic fruits of both good and evil ripen, they must first be repaid.
Thus, one cycles through the seven destinies, sinking forever into the ocean of suffering. The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* states:

"Though one may attain the body of a Great Brahmā Heaven, even reaching the very summit of the triple world and living for eighty-four thousand great kalpas, if one does not realize the wondrously enlightened mind, the five signs of decay will appear."

They fall back once again into the realms of suffering. Viewed from this perspective, even those who have attained the state of an immortal remain, in the eyes of the Buddha, ordinary worldlings who have not yet transcended birth and death.
Only the Buddha is the Great King of Physicians, capable of healing all the poisons of worldly suffering and afflictions.
If one wishes to escape the net of suffering, there is no other way than to dwell in reliance upon the Buddha, dwell in reliance upon the Dharma, and dwell in reliance upon the Sangha.
Diligently cultivate pure karma and keep Amitābha in mind at every thought. As a result, you will attain rebirth in Sukhāvatī and be forever severed from the three realms.
Once this is accomplished, everything is resolved; do not harbor any lingering doubts.
If one has already understood the Dharma-gate of the Pure Land, it is especially necessary to clearly comprehend the two causes—the primary and the auxiliary.

The primary cause is the recitation of the Buddha's name; the auxiliary cause is the observance of the precepts. The gateway of the precepts is vast, yet it takes the five fundamental precepts as its general framework:

namely, the precept against killing, the precept against stealing, the precept against sexual misconduct, the precept against false speech, and the precept against drinking intoxicants. Once these five precepts are fully established, naturally...
"Be able to refrain from all evil and practice all that is good. These two phrases originate from the *Yinzhi Wen* (Text on Secret Merits) of Emperor Wen Chang.
Formerly, when Master Lianchi was the mainstay of the Pure Land school, famous officials and high-ranking dignitaries gathered like clouds to take refuge in him.
He would often say: "The *Yinzhi Wen* is for this world; the *Amitabha Sutra* is for the world beyond. Now, even those in the secular world know this.
When reciting the *Yinyi* (Text on Karmic Retribution), one often regards the two lines—"Commit no evil; practice all good"—as mere platitudes heard from old men.
Yet, as the Chan Master Niaoke once said: "The two lines 'Commit no evil;
practice all good' can be spoken by a three-year-old child, yet cannot be practiced by a hundred-year-old man. How profound these words are! In the *Āgama Sūtras*, Ānanda...
The Venerable One also said: "One should know that all evils must not be committed, and all good deeds should be practiced.
Long ago, when the Bodhisattva Subhūti was diligently seeking the Buddha-dharma, he encountered a woman who appeared like a manifestation of the Buddha.
The Bodhisattva Subhūti prostrated himself in reverence, and the woman replied: "The wondrous Dharma of the Buddhas is immeasurable and boundless; what I have heard is but a single half-verse. All...
"Do no evil; practice all that is good. Upon hearing this, Subhūti’s body and mind became pure, and he thoroughly penetrated its profound meaning.
One can see that practicing good and refraining from evil constitute the very foundation of the path to cultivation. If this foundation is not established, the sprouts of goodness will not flourish.
For those who practice the recitation of the Buddha's name, observing these two phrases serves as a supporting cause, like a ship encountering a favorable wind that swiftly reaches its destination.
One has reached the other shore.
The reason people are unwilling to seek birth in the Pure Land is that they do not know the suffering of retribution in hell is both severe and long-lasting.

This includes all those in the world who are great villains and evildoers, those who are disloyal and unfilial, those who pierce the body of the Buddha with blood, and those who defile and violate monks and nuns.
Those who obstruct others from leaving the household life and destroy their resolve for the Path fall into the Avīci Hell.
In this hell, they suffer without interruption, with no time of release. The *Kṣitigarbha-pūrvapraṇidhāna-sūtra* states: "When this world-system is destroyed, one is reborn in another world-system;

when that world-system is next destroyed, one is transferred to yet another region; when that region is destroyed, one is successively transferred elsewhere. After this world-system is reformed, one returns once more."
They come [to this state]. When heaven and earth undergo transformation and destruction, yet sinful karma knows no end. The offenses of the Avīci Hell are as heavy as this;

while the retribution for other evil deeds may not last as long, there is no one among sentient beings who can escape the consequences of the three karmas of body, speech, and mind committed during their lifetimes.
Once the retribution in hell is exhausted, they will depart with lingering wounds.

Having killed living beings, one must repay each life taken in full before one can act for the sake of those who are poor, suffering, and lowly. If one plants merit through this, one will immediately receive a reward of fortune.
Yet once that reward of fortune is obtained, it becomes easier to commit evil; a single lapse may cause one's stubbornly accumulated merit to be exhausted, leading once again to a fall from grace.
Among these, there are cases where one descends from wealth and status to poverty and meanness, or changes from a male body to a female body.
From the hells one goes to the animal realm; rising and falling, high and low, one revolves without end.
Observing this, it is truly and certainly that the realms of hell exist, and there is truly and certainly a body that undergoes retribution.

If you harbor both faith and doubt, or are indolent and lax, then when evil accumulates and retribution arrives in a single day, it will be difficult to ensure that you do not share in the fate of hell. If you say, "I still have merit, so let me enjoy it for now," [you are mistaken].

Some commit evil and yet wait for retribution to arrive; they incur further punishment for their transgressions. I fear that when the blade, the saw, the cauldron, and the boiling pot stand before me, it will be too late for regret.
Generally, those who fall into the Avīci Hell have their consciousnesses clouded and deluded;
though they wish to recite the Buddha’s name, their karmic power obstructs them so that not a single syllable can escape their lips. How terrifying this is!
Within the four continents under heaven, it is only in Jambudvīpa in the south that the human mind is most wicked; killing, stealing, lust, and lying ceaselessly throughout the day.
Yet, from antiquity, those who have attained Buddhahood or become patriarchs have mostly appeared here. Why is this?

It is because the human mind is sharp and vigorous, making it easy to give rise to the genuine aspiration for the Way, unlike the people of other continents, whose cultivation of the ten wholesome deeds results only in rebirth in the heavens.
The Sūtra states: "The people of the Western Continent commit only minor evils, yet to this day their customs remain sincere and generous, and their lifespan is one thousand years.
However, because they ultimately do not believe in the Buddha-dharma, although they may attain birth in the heavens, they have still not escaped saṃsāra.

Observing this, one realizes that to avoid the hells, it is impossible without practicing goodness; to escape saṃsāra, it is impossible without practicing the Pure Land method of nianfo (Buddha-recitation)."

By reciting the Buddha’s name, one can immediately give rise to the true mind of the Way. Once this true mind of the Way has been awakened, one attains Buddhahood and becomes an ancestral patriarch, directly taking up the responsibility;
is this not the true hero of the world?

In this world, there are those who perform good deeds in their current life yet encounter adverse conditions; there are also those who commit evil in their current life yet enjoy fortunate retributions.
Consequently, they act with utter arrogance, claiming that fortune and calamity have no basis and that karmic retribution is inverted, thereby utterly dismissing the doctrine of cause and effect.
Little do they realize that in the netherworld, between the two retributions of merit and sin, whichever has ripened first must be repaid. It is, for example, like planting...

Regarding trees: those planted earlier will first flower and bear fruit; those planted recently, despite being nurtured with double the effort, cannot immediately provide shade, nor can they flower and bear fruit at once.
This is the very principle [at work]. Master Wang Longshu said:

"When people see that good and evil deeds do not yet yield retribution in the present, they consequently fail to believe in cause and effect; and because they do not believe in cause and effect, they do not believe in the Pure Land."

Little do people realize that when good or evil deeds have not yet yielded their retribution, it is not that there is no retribution; it is merely a matter of whether it is delayed or swift. Long ago, the Buddha said to Ānanda:
"There are those who perform good deeds in this life yet fall into hell after death; there are also those who perform evil deeds in this life [yet attain a fortunate rebirth]."
Regarding those who die and are reborn in the heavenly realms, Ānanda asked for the reason. The Buddha said:

"Those who perform good deeds in this life but fall into hell after death are such that the good karma of this life has not yet ripened, while the evil karma of their previous lives has already ripened.

Those who commit evil deeds in this life but are reborn in the heavenly realms after death are such that the evil karma of this life has not yet ripened, while the good karma of their previous lives has already ripened. Wherever the karma has ripened, one first receives the retribution there."
It is like a debt: when one is in urgent need, it must be repaid first. When the resonance between cause and response intersects, there can be no confusion regarding priority or sequence.

Yet, ordinary people, their eyes of karma obstructed, cannot clearly perceive the hidden realms. Consequently, they dismiss as a whole the teachings on cause and effect, mindfulness of the Buddha, and so forth.
Having lost faith themselves, they further teach others not to believe. This single moment of error, this single word—
These are delusions. The karmic retribution of the mouth is boundless; it secretly diminishes one’s hidden virtues and serves as the very root of the hells.

If one can develop deep faith in cause and effect, the mindfulness of the Buddha will arise spontaneously. By proceeding directly forward from this point, it will not be difficult to clarify the mind and realize one's nature.
Will the people of the world also acknowledge my bitter words?
One should know that for the direct and swift method of cultivating the path, none is equal to the recitation of the Buddha's name.

This Dharma-door of Buddha-recitation was pointed out by the Tathāgata as a skillful means for sentient beings who are timid and weak during the age of the Final Dharma (*mappō*). This door completely encompasses and gathers all within it.
This is most extraordinary and marvelous. It can lead one out of the burning house of the triple world and uproot the intense sufferings of the three miserable realms.
By diligently cultivating merit and goodness, one may barely attain birth in the heavens; yet once celestial blessings are exhausted, one inevitably falls back down.

Only by reciting the Buddha's name and attaining rebirth in the Pure Land can one fulfill the rank of a Buddha in a single lifetime. It should be known that if one slanders it or lacks faith, one will fall forever into hell. Namo Amitābha.
The six characters of the name of Amitābha Buddha possess vast merit and inconceivable power. It is difficult to encounter the True Dharma in this present life;
therefore, one should be willing to sacrifice body and life and recite it with all one’s might.

Although the roots of goodness of sentient beings vary in thickness, it is like sifting gold from sand: those with sharp faculties and abundant merit will naturally attain clarity of vision and wisdom early on.
It can be attained. That is, even those of dull faculties and inferior wisdom, provided they are able to seek diligently without slackening, may gather it bit by bit;
they will not return empty-handed. If there are like-minded companions, they will surely not find these words obscure or nonsensical.
Formerly, He Shangzhi addressed Emperor Ming of the Song dynasty, saying: "In a village of a hundred households, if one person observes the five precepts, then that one person becomes virtuous;
if ten people observe the five precepts, then those ten people become virtuous. To practice one good deed is to eliminate one evil; to eliminate one evil is to eliminate one punishment.
When one punishment ceases within a household, ten thousand punishments cease within the state. Your Majesty can thus achieve this while sitting at ease."

All is at peace. It can be seen that upholding the precepts and believing in the Buddha is not only an essential method for transcending the world, but also an excellent remedy for governing the world.
I wish that those who read books and understand principle would believe in and uphold this, so as not to commit the karma of slander.
I know this man; he must have already deeply mastered the arts of cultivation and attained thorough penetration of phenomena and principle.
Tired of the mundane world, he has traced back several decades of his arduous resolve in studying the Way. I have composed eight seven-character quatrains for him. Not... [end of fragment]
I venture to speak of poetry; it is merely to dispel my weariness.

Furthermore, I urge those of us practicing together who have been young to carry their books and follow the instructions of a teacher, for I deeply hope that the legacy of literary excellence will continue the tradition of the sages of old. Suddenly, in middle age, the world fell into chaos;
in a state of panic, we took a single boat to flee the smoke of war.
From now on I shall dwell in a desolate village; casting aside the bamboo slips and leather bindings, I attend to the wine jar. Those we encounter by chance are all but cowherds;
from where, then, can one inquire about the source of the mind?

The passage of time is like a swift arrow; in these twenty-four hours, may we meet with the conditions for the Lotus and be encouraged to practice. Though the name of the mind does not weary, it is like a bird returning to its forest;
though the Great Way is clear, one still harbors doubts in secret.

I have repeatedly received many letters from my spiritual mentors, who urge me to abandon my vexations and attachments like wielding the Great Sword. There is only the Dharma of the Jewel King Samādhi;
I shall cultivate the Pure Land horizontally and recite the name of Amitābha.
From this point, I have searched through the texts on the Pure Land; now, with a single stroke of the morning bell reaching my ears, I finally realize that this illusory body is entirely false.
I sigh deeply at how the fragrant oil was burned in vain.
In this Sahā world, the path of study is most difficult to accomplish; planting lotuses amidst fire requires cherishing the true.
Only when iron walls and copper fortifications remain unshaken can one finally let go of the hand and emerge from the red dust of the mundane world.
Dust and mist shall not cause the mirror-stand to be sealed. Blending with the world and harmonizing with light throughout this life, I am fortunate that the monkey’s tether can be firmly restrained;
six times a day, I gaze upon the red glow of the Buddha-lamp.
Fifty years of dense and profound contemplation within my heart; at the sunset on the edge of the sea, I gaze toward the western heavens. My family has always belonged to the Lotus Land;
crossing upon a single reed, I have come to the East to fulfill the karmic conditions for saving the world.
Record of the Arousing of Faith Compiled by Master Lianxiu, Scroll Six (End)
